title: After the release an organization has the categories and the setting off
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use the production test account.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, named like the shop's own fleet, with one open billable work order, work order 1, made before the release.
custom_steps:
1. Open Administration > Service > Internal Work Orders.
  2. Open Settings > Work Orders.
  3. Open customer A's page.
  4. Open work order 1.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • General Internal (Default), Warranty, Goodwill and Comeback are listed once each; Warranty and Comeback show "Required".

Step 2:

  • The "Internal Work Orders" toggle is off and no hint line shows under it.

Step 3:

  • Customer A shows no "Internal" badge: no customer was flagged.

Step 4:

  • Work order 1 is still billable, with no badge, and offers "Create invoice".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories), story SV-12295 (Story 13, Release day, seeding and migration)

  • S13-R1: “A one-time migration creates the starting categories for every organization (S1-R13): General Internal as the default Internal category; Warranty, Goodwill and Comeback as No Charge categories, with Requires the original work order on for Warranty and Comeback. Nothing is created in QuickBooks and nothing is turned on: the Internal Work Orders setting stays off for every organization.”
  • S13-R5: “Verification after the run, per organization: four categories, four QuickBooks rows per connected location, four hub mappings populated (Comeback included), the setting off. The rule-zero verify of S9-R14 runs the same day. If engineering ships the feature behind a deploy switch until launch day, the switch is removed with the launch and is not a product setting (Key Decisions, No feature flag).”
  • S13-R6: “Shops that keep an "Internal" or "Shop Fleet" customer today are not touched: the migration flags no customer and reclassifies no work order (Assumptions); S1-R11 handles it when the shop flags the customer.”
  • Feature Overview: “Two kinds of work order, one way to close them.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

AUTOMATION: HOLD - needs records and figures noted on production before the release reaches production; run on production after the release
